D: A weatherman relives the same day over and over in Punxsutawney.
P: Serve the breakfast feast when Phil gorges at the diner.
S: Tip Top Cafe silver dollar pancakes
the diner Phil goes to every single day

Little buttermilk pancakes cooked in butter until golden, stacked high with whipped maple butter, crisp bacon bits and a drizzle of warm maple syrup. Whisk 250g self-raising flour, 2 tbsp caster sugar and a pinch of salt with 375ml buttermilk, 2 eggs and 40g melted butter. Rest 15 minutes. Beat 80g soft butter with 2 tbsp maple syrup. Fry 150g diced bacon until crisp. Cook tablespoons of batter in a buttered pan over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes a side. Stack, top with the maple butter and bacon bits, and pour over warm maple syrup.
the festival in the town square
Cake doughnuts warmed at 160C for 2 minutes, then shaken in a paper bag with cinnamon sugar until coated.
Eggs boiled 10 minutes, yolks whipped with mayo, Dijon, a dash of hot sauce and paprika, piped back into the whites.
M: pancakes, eggs, bacon, toast and pie, everything at once
Bacon rendered crisp, fried eggs, a short stack, buttered toast and a slice of pie, all on the table at the same time.
the town's Groundhog Day party at the end of the night

Golden roast chicken with sage and onion stuffing, creamy mashed potato, buttered green beans and a rich pan gravy, small-town dinner dance style. Rub a 1.8kg chicken with salt the night before. Roast at 220C for 20 minutes, then 180C for 50 minutes until the thigh reaches 75C, and rest. Mix 150g breadcrumbs with 1 onion softened in 50g butter, chopped sage, 1 egg and stock, then bake in a dish for 30 minutes. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and 100ml milk. Make gravy from the pan juices with 1 tbsp flour and 300ml stock. Steam 300g green beans.
W: Phil orders it with everything else

Whisk 10 egg whites with cream of tartar to soft peaks, add 150g sugar, fold in 120g cake flour sifted with 150g icing sugar, bake in an ungreased tube pan at 175C for 40 minutes, cool upside down. Berries and cream.
K: Rita's sweet vermouth on the rocks
Rita's order at the bar, with a twist, to world peace

Sweet red vermouth poured over a big block of ice with a long twist of orange peel and a dash of bitters, exactly as Rita orders it. Put one large ice block in each of 4 rocks glasses. Pour 75ml sweet red vermouth over each and add a dash of aromatic bitters. Peel 4 long strips of orange zest, twist each over the glass to release the oil, rub round the rim and drop in. Stir twice. Totals are 300ml vermouth and 1 orange. Raise a glass to world peace.

edition.cue: Serve the breakfast feast when Phil gorges at the diner.

s.note: Warm cake doughnuts shaken in a paper bag with cinnamon sugar.
s.how: Warm 4 small plain cake doughnuts at 160°C conventional for 2 minutes. Put 30g caster sugar and 1/2 tsp cinnamon in a clean food-safe paper bag. Add the warm doughnuts and shake gently until coated. Serve one each.

s.note: Boiled egg halves with creamy mustard yolks, hot sauce and paprika.
s.how: Boil 4 eggs for 10 minutes, cool in iced water and peel. Halve and remove the yolks. Whip the yolks with 30g mayonnaise, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, 1/2 tsp hot sauce and 1/4 tsp smoked paprika until smooth. Pipe back into the eight white halves and refrigerate until serving.

m.note: Crisp bacon, fried eggs, pancakes, buttered toast and a slice of pie.
m.how: Mix 150g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 15g caster sugar, 1 egg and 200ml buttermilk into a batter. Rest 15 minutes. Render 200g bacon slowly in a frying pan over medium heat for 10 minutes until crisp and keep warm. Cook eight small pancakes in 20g butter for about 2 minutes per side until bubbles set and both sides are golden. Fry 4 eggs in the bacon pan for 3 minutes, or until the whites are set. Toast 4 slices white bread and butter with 20g butter. Warm four small 50g slices ready-baked pie at 180°C for 10 minutes. Bring everything to the table at once, with 60ml maple syrup for the pancakes.

w.note: Light egg white sponge with fresh berries and softly whipped cream.
w.how: Whisk 5 egg whites with 1/4 tsp cream of tartar to soft peaks. Gradually add 75g caster sugar and whisk until glossy. Sift 60g cake flour with 75g icing sugar, then gently fold into the whites in three additions. Spoon into an ungreased 16cm tube pan. Bake at 175°C conventional for 40 minutes until golden and springy. Invert the tin and cool upside down completely before loosening the cake. Cut into four portions and serve with 150g fresh berries and 80ml thickened cream softly whipped.
